identityScreen: All 151 active identities screened. Relevant humanities, sociology, politics, economics, business, media and language leads read substantively below; technical/life/environment unrelated fields cannot supply absent Chinese disciplinary content merely through project freedom.
conceptBeforeSelection: Strongest closest response: historical and contemporary inquiry into China’s political economy, society and cultural representation, using comparative historical, political, social and literary methods. Retain Chinese source/language and disciplinary regional inquiry as target, not a generic global affairs degree.
status: Provisional academic challenge only. No valid comparison or no-match is certified while the external language allocation is unresolved.
positiveCase: Specific ancient China/empires, Asian-American exclusion/diaspora, authoritarianism/civil society, international trade, growth, AI industrial policy and qualitative/media/text methods are genuine connections. The negative consideration is programme-level sustained China-centred inquiry, not a missing title/language quota, a matching-course count or absence of enrichment.
challengeResult: The 24-course palette is coherent as global politics/economy/culture, but would rely on freely selected projects to make China its continuing object. Many concrete complements are justified to that general concept, while the concept-to-target relation remains materially weak. Preserve this concern for final comparability when the external blocker is resolved; do not publish a no-match from the unresolved source case.
candidateStopping: No additional alternative is approved. Political-economy and cultural directions have distinct substantive bases but do not bypass the first-comparison gate; language/text direction lacks actual Chinese-language teaching in current active catalogue. No arbitrary four-course changes or three-slot target.

courses.name: Personal & Professional Development
courses.judgment: Mandatory PPD exemption; not evidence of Chinese-studies subject coverage.

courses.name: Modern History
courses.judgment: Modernity, imperialism, revolution and global change provide specific historical frameworks, but no sustained modern China sequence is specified.

courses.name: History of Empires
courses.judgment: Positive direct bridge: comparative empires explicitly include ancient China and modern Asian empires; partial Chinese historical inquiry, not merely a global title. Not the complete premodern/modern China progression.

courses.name: Introduction to Political Philosophy
courses.judgment: Political authority, socialism/communism, empire and non-European thinkers support political interpretation; no documented sustained Chinese political-text or institutional sequence.

courses.name: Foundations of Comparative Politics
courses.judgment: Authoritarianism, parties, institutions and political economy directly support analytical questions of governing China. Empirical comparison is valuable; actual China application is not guaranteed.

courses.name: Theory of International Relations
courses.judgment: Great-power competition, geopolitics, economic relations and country-position research materially support the China/global-affairs direction. No compulsory China country focus inferred.

courses.name: Public Policy Analysis
courses.judgment: Description-only course fully considered: globalization, sugar case and policy memos are real policy training. They do not establish Chinese policy cases or more detailed methods than the description states.

courses.name: Peace & Conflict
courses.judgment: Conflict, identity, colonial legacies and policy analysis are concrete complementary tools for China/world relations; project freedom does not establish Chinese conflict or society coverage.

courses.name: Introduction to Sociology
courses.judgment: Modernity, class, inequality, identity and migration give relevant theoretical foundations for social change in China; not Chinese family/hukou/danwei inquiry itself.

courses.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
courses.judgment: Actual qualitative design, interviews, ethnography and documentary analysis are relevant disciplinary research training; neither Mandarin source access nor a Chinese field site is required.

courses.name: Modern Sociology
courses.judgment: Critical modernity, Eurocentrism, Bourdieu and postcolonial theory can support China/modernity interpretation. Do not relabel general theories as sinology.

courses.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
courses.judgment: Civil society under authoritarianism and digital publics offer a specific contemporary-politics bridge, but documented civil-society projects have no sustained China requirement.

courses.name: Introduction to Economics
courses.judgment: Real market and macroeconomic foundations support understanding Chinese development. Not evidence of Chinese reform history.

courses.name: International Macroeconomics
courses.judgment: Growth, open economy and policy analysis materially support China/global-economic questions. It does not supply China’s actual institutional transformation.

courses.name: International Business & Governance
courses.judgment: Trade, FDI, monetary systems and governance form a strong specific international-economic response. Country/market project could concern China but is not documented as doing so.

courses.name: Transnational Business Law
courses.judgment: Cross-border trade, investment and digital business law are concrete complements to external economic relations; not Chinese law or business culture.

courses.name: Business & Economy in the Age of AI
courses.judgment: AI labour/industrial-policy/regulation and country-readiness project materially connect to the actual Chinese AI-politics elective. Does not guarantee Chinese state governance, surveillance or political ideology.

courses.name: Introduction to Literary Studies
courses.judgment: Close reading, narrative and adaptation teach relevant literary methods, but not Chinese literature or Classical Chinese texts.

courses.name: World Myth & Literature
courses.judgment: Actual comparative myth corpus includes Indian, Arabic, African and Mediterranean traditions; cultural transmission is real, but Chinese Journey-to-the-West coverage is not stated.

courses.name: Film & Text
courses.judgment: Film/text adaptation is a relevant analytic practice for the target’s cultural direction. No actual Chinese adaptation corpus established.

courses.name: Perspectives on Literary Meaning
courses.judgment: Description-only perspectives and interpretive research receive full consideration. They support literary inquiry without establishing Chinese texts or cultural history.

courses.name: Introduction to Film & Media
courses.judgment: Close film/media interpretation, representation and postcolonial approaches provide genuine relevant methods. They do not establish Chinese media institutions/content.

courses.name: Media & Race
courses.judgment: Positive China/diaspora-adjacent subject: Asian-American exclusion in American media history, alongside race/representation and archives. This is acknowledged, but Japanese incarceration and general American race history must not be presented as a Chinese-studies sequence.

courses.name: The Documentary
courses.judgment: Documentary analysis, ethnography and interviewing materially support cultural/societal research practice; no required China object or fieldwork.

courses.name: Histories of Gender
courses.judgment: North American gender and queer histories: transferable intersectional/oral-history practice, not Chinese gender history. Do not use the MeToo example to invent a taught Chinese case.

courses.name: Ways of War
courses.judgment: Western warfare and strategic primary-source analysis: specific military methods, but no documented Battle-of-Guningtou/Chinese military history. An illustrative thesis cannot generate this substitution.

courses.name: Researching the “American Century”
courses.judgment: Description-only historical research receives full consideration: inquiry, source critique and research paper are substantive. No China corpus may be inferred from the short description or title.

courses.name: Social Movements & Environmental Justice
courses.judgment: Description-only environmental justice/social movement case analysis is relevant complementary method; no Chinese civic movement specified.

courses.name: Great Literary Works
courses.judgment: Specific world-literary corpus and motifs offer comparative context; no sustained Chinese canon stated.

courses.name: Life & Travel Writing
courses.judgment: Migration/language/identity and memoir research have a real diaspora bridge; China-specific corpus not established.

courses.name: Media Archaeology
courses.judgment: Print, material media and transmission practices are relevant methods; no Chinese media history documented.

courses.name: From T.V. to TikTok
courses.judgment: American media and identity have substantive content, but its American focus cannot be renamed Chinese popular culture.

courses.name: Media & the Environment
courses.judgment: Ecocritical media inquiry could support global environment questions, but neither Chinese media nor an environment generator is compulsory in this target.

courses.name: Introduction to World Archaeology
courses.judgment: World archaeology genuinely includes Asia and material-culture methods. It is a positive global/comparative lead, not enough to establish Chinese dynastic art/history progression.

courses.name: African Art & Heritage
courses.judgment: African visual traditions, heritage and restitution are real but concern another regional object; China/Africa trade relations do not turn this into Chinese art.

courses.name: Modern Art & Modern Museums
courses.judgment: Global contemporary art, museums and Eurocentrism are genuine bridges; no documented sustained Chinese visual culture.

courses.name: Introduction to Western Philosophy
courses.judgment: Western philosophy plus Buddhist self theory supplies an acknowledged Asian connection, not Chinese Confucian/Daoist philosophical traditions.

courses.name: Ethics
courses.judgment: Ethical argumentation from specified Western traditions complements inquiry, not Chinese philosophy itself.

courses.name: Free Will, Time & the Self
courses.judgment: Greek and Indian agency/self debates acknowledged; no Chinese tradition inferred from Asian geography.

courses.name: Psycholinguistics
courses.judgment: Description-only neurobiological language processing, acquisition, bilingualism and experiments fully considered. Does not teach Mandarin/classical reading, Chinese linguistics or translation. A real course, not disqualified for absent outline.
